codes.d: No row was found that satisfies the search condition, or the result of a FETCH was past the last row of the cursor result table.
codes.a: A SELECT INTO, UPDATE, DELETE, or FETCH found zero matching rows.
codes.f: Check WHERE clause logic. Treat +100 as a normal end-of-data condition for cursor loops. Always test SQLCODE = 100 after fetches.
codes.x:
EXEC SQL
   FETCH C1 INTO :EMPNO, :NAME
END-EXEC.
IF SQLCODE = 100
   PERFORM CLOSE-CURSOR.

codes.d: Trying to fetch a row from a scrollable cursor where the row has been deleted (an update or delete hole).
codes.a: Another transaction deleted or updated the underlying row of a SENSITIVE STATIC scrollable cursor.
codes.f: Skip to the next row, or re-execute the query to refresh the result table.
codes.x: EXEC SQL FETCH RELATIVE +1 FROM C1 INTO :V END-EXEC.

codes.t: VALUE CANNOT BE ASSIGNED - OUT OF RANGE
codes.d: A value with data type cannot be assigned to a host variable because it is out of range.
codes.a: Target host variable cannot represent the column value (e.g., SMALLINT host variable receiving INTEGER value).
codes.f: Use a host variable with sufficient range and matching data type. Add an indicator variable to detect truncation.
codes.x: 01 V-NUM PIC S9(4) COMP.    *> too small for INTEGER column

codes.d: A character could not be converted and was substituted by the substitution character.
codes.a: Code page conversion encountered a character with no equivalent in the target CCSID.
codes.f: Verify CCSID of source and target. Use compatible encodings or sanitize input data before storing.
codes.x: SELECT NAME FROM EMP WHERE CCSID 1208 -> CCSID 37

codes.d: A character has been substituted during input conversion.
codes.a: Character set conversion is incomplete or lossy.
codes.f: Ensure consistent CCSIDs across client and server. Avoid mixing single-byte and multi-byte character sets.
codes.x: Client CCSID 1208 sending DBCS to host CCSID 37.

codes.d: The SQL statement has been successfully executed but a problem with DRDA character conversion may exist.
codes.a: Different CCSID encoding rules between an ASCII-based DRDA client and EBCDIC DB2 for z/OS.
codes.f: Confirm CCSID negotiation succeeded. Set ENCODING bind option to match application data.
codes.x: BIND PLAN(PLN) MEMBER(PGM) ENCODING(EBCDIC)

codes.t: ASSIGNMENT TO TRANSITION VARIABLE NOT ALLOWED
codes.d: Assignment to a transition variable that corresponds to a non-updatable column is ignored.
codes.a: A trigger SET tried to update a generated, identity, or ROWID column via NEW transition variable.
codes.f: Remove the assignment in the trigger body. Use a regular UPDATE to modify these columns.
codes.x:
CREATE TRIGGER T1 BEFORE INSERT ON EMP
  REFERENCING NEW AS N FOR EACH ROW
  SET N.EMPID = 0;   /* ignored if EMPID is GENERATED ALWAYS */

codes.d: User specified optimization hints were used during access path selection.
codes.a: Statement included QUERYNO and OPTHINT, and DB2 found a valid plan in PLAN_TABLE.
codes.f: Informational only. Verify the hint's access path matches your intent via EXPLAIN.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE EMPNO=:H OPTIMIZE FOR 1 ROW QUERYNO 100;

codes.d: Value has been truncated by a CAST function.
codes.a: CAST shortened a longer string to a smaller target length.
codes.f: Increase the target length or trim/validate input before casting. Test with indicator variables for truncation.
codes.x: SELECT CAST(NAME AS CHAR(5)) FROM EMP;  /* truncates names > 5 */

codes.d: External function or procedure has returned a warning SQLSTATE.
codes.a: A UDF or stored procedure invoked from SQL returned a non-zero SQLSTATE starting with '01'.
codes.f: Inspect the SQLSTATE returned by the routine. Update the routine to clear warnings if expected behavior.
codes.x: CALL MYPROC(:IN, :OUT);  /* routine returned 01HXX SQLSTATE */

codes.d: Exception error has occurred during the performance of an arithmetic operation or data conversion.
codes.a: Result of an arithmetic expression overflowed the data type; division by zero; or NULL produced.
codes.f: Validate operands. Use CASE to handle divide-by-zero. Cast to a larger type before computation.
codes.x: SELECT SALARY * 100 FROM EMP;  /* overflows SMALLINT result */

codes.d: The statement contains the illegal character that is not permitted in an SQL statement.
codes.a: Non-printable or unsupported character (e.g., binary zero, control char) embedded in SQL text.
codes.f: Edit the SQL source and remove the offending character. Check the host variable for binary data.
codes.x: EXEC SQL SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE NAME=':X^@'  END-EXEC.

codes.d: The SQL statement contains a string constant, beginning with a character, that is not terminated properly.
codes.a: Missing closing apostrophe on a literal.
codes.f: Add the missing terminating quote. Escape embedded quotes by doubling them ('' for ').
codes.x: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE NAME = 'SMITH;   /* missing ' */

codes.d: INTO clause is required for the SELECT statement when it is used in a host program.
codes.a: Static embedded SELECT without an INTO clause for host variables.
codes.f: Add INTO :host-var-list to the static SELECT, or declare and use a cursor for multi-row results.
codes.x: EXEC SQL SELECT EMPNO FROM EMP WHERE WORKDEPT='A00' END-EXEC.  /* missing INTO */

codes.d: Name has been previously declared.
codes.a: Same SQL identifier (cursor, statement, table name) declared twice in the same scope.
codes.f: Rename one occurrence or delete the duplicate DECLARE.
codes.x:
EXEC SQL DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR ... END-EXEC.
EXEC SQL DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR ... END-EXEC.

codes.d: Invalid type specification on a CAST, function invocation, or COLUMN reference.
codes.a: Misspelled data type, missing precision/scale, or invalid length.
codes.f: Correct the data type per DB2 SQL Reference. For example DECIMAL(p,s), VARCHAR(n).
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T (C1 DECIMAL(35,2));  /* precision > max */

codes.d: An SQL statement is not allowed in this context.
codes.a: Statement type prohibited in the runtime environment (e.g., DDL in a stored procedure that disallows it).
codes.f: Move the statement to an allowed context, or check the bind options used for the program.
codes.x: CALL SP_QUERY(:X);  /* SP attempts CREATE TABLE but bound DISALLOW DEBUG */

codes.d: The use of LONG VARCHAR or LONG VARGRAPHIC data type is not allowed in this statement.
codes.a: LONG VARCHAR columns can't be used in indexes, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, or DISTINCT clauses.
codes.f: Cast to VARCHAR(n) where n is allowed, or restructure the query to not use the column in those clauses.
codes.x: SELECT DISTINCT NOTES FROM EMP;  /* NOTES is LONG VARCHAR */

codes.t: STATEMENT TOO LONG OR TOO COMPLEX
codes.d: The statement is too long or too complex to be processed.
codes.a: SQL text or its parsed form exceeded DB2 internal limits (e.g., too many tables joined, expressions, predicates).
codes.f: Split the query into smaller statements, use views, or temp tables. Reduce IN-list size.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM T1, T2, ... , T255;  /* exceeds join limit */

codes.d: A string constant or delimited identifier exceeds the maximum length permitted.
codes.a: Literal longer than 32704 bytes (or 32672 for VARCHAR).
codes.f: Store the value in a host variable instead of a literal, or split into multiple inserts.
codes.x: INSERT INTO NOTES VALUES ('A'||'A'||...32K times);

codes.d: The numeric literal is not valid because of its value or format.
codes.a: Number out of range, contains invalid character, or has wrong format (e.g., '1.2.3', '1E').
codes.f: Re-enter the literal in valid numeric form. Use a string literal with CAST if needed.
codes.x: SELECT 1E FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.d: An illegal symbol or token was encountered in the SQL statement at the position indicated.
codes.a: Misspelled keyword, missing comma, extra word, or reserved word used as identifier.
codes.f: Read the position pointer in the message. Correct the syntax around that token.
codes.x: SELECT FROM EMP;  /* missing column list */

codes.d: A string constant beginning with a special character (X, GX, BX, etc.) is invalid.
codes.a: Hex/graphic/binary literal has invalid characters or wrong number of digits.
codes.f: Ensure hex literals have even digit count; graphic literals use valid DBCS pairs.
codes.x: SELECT X'1G' FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;  /* G not hex */

codes.d: The name is too long. Maximum allowable size is a specified length.
codes.a: Identifier exceeds DB2 max length (e.g., 128 for table names, 30 for cursors).
codes.f: Shorten the identifier.
codes.x: DECLARE THIS_IS_AN_EXTREMELY_LONG_CURSOR_NAME CURSOR FOR SELECT 1;

codes.d: The name is qualified incorrectly.
codes.a: Too many or wrong qualifiers (e.g., LOCATION.SCHEMA.TABLE.COL in invalid context).
codes.f: Use the qualifier form expected (schema.object or location.schema.object).
codes.x: SELECT MYDB.SCHEMA.EMP.NAME FROM MYDB.SCHEMA.EMP;

codes.d: The clause is not permitted in this context.
codes.a: ORDER BY in subquery, INTO in dynamic SQL, ORDER BY in a view, etc.
codes.f: Remove the disallowed clause or rewrite the statement.
codes.x: CREATE VIEW V AS SELECT * FROM EMP ORDER BY NAME;

codes.d: Invalid hexadecimal literal beginning with the indicated character.
codes.a: Hex literal contains a non-hex digit or has an odd number of digits.
codes.f: Use only 0-9 and A-F, in pairs.
codes.x: SELECT X'ABC' FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;  /* odd length */

codes.t: COLUMN FUNCTION REQUIRES A QUALIFIED COLUMN
codes.d: A column function does not include a column name.
codes.a: Aggregate (SUM, MAX, etc.) was used without specifying a column reference.
codes.f: Provide a column expression inside the aggregate, e.g., SUM(SALARY).
codes.x: SELECT SUM(*) FROM EMP;

codes.t: OPERAND OF COLUMN FUNCTION INCLUDES A COLUMN FUNCTION
codes.d: The operand of a column function is another column function.
codes.a: Nested aggregates like MAX(SUM(SAL)) are not allowed directly.
codes.f: Use a subquery or CTE: SELECT MAX(S) FROM (SELECT SUM(SAL) AS S FROM EMP GROUP BY DEPT).
codes.x: SELECT MAX(SUM(SALARY)) FROM EMP;

codes.d: Invalid character found in name or string.
codes.a: Identifier or string contains a character not allowed by DB2.
codes.f: Use only valid characters (letters, digits, underscores). Delimit with double quotes if needed.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE EMP-DATA (C1 INT);  /* hyphen not allowed */

codes.t: NUMBER OF VALUES NOT EQUAL TO NUMBER OF COLUMNS
codes.d: The number of values to be assigned is not the same as the number of specified or implied columns.
codes.a: INSERT VALUES list count doesn't match column list (or implicit table column count).
codes.f: Match each column with a value; provide an explicit column list to be safe.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(EMPNO, NAME) VALUES (10);

codes.t: DELETE/UPDATE TABLE ALSO IDENTIFIED IN FROM CLAUSE
codes.d: The object table of the DELETE or UPDATE statement is also identified in a FROM clause.
codes.a: Target table referenced in the FROM clause of the WHERE subquery.
codes.f: Use a correlated subquery on a copy of the table, or use MERGE.
codes.x: DELETE FROM EMP WHERE SAL < (SELECT AVG(SAL) FROM EMP);

codes.t: COLUMN IN HAVING CLAUSE NOT IN GROUP BY
codes.d: A column identified in a HAVING clause is not included in the GROUP BY clause.
codes.a: HAVING references a column outside of an aggregate that isn't in GROUP BY.
codes.f: Add the column to GROUP BY or wrap it in an aggregate function.
codes.x: SELECT DEPT, MAX(SAL) FROM EMP GROUP BY DEPT HAVING JOB = 'MGR';

codes.t: WHERE/SET CLAUSE CONTAINS A COLUMN FUNCTION
codes.d: A WHERE clause or SET clause includes a column function in an invalid context.
codes.a: Aggregate used outside HAVING or SELECT list.
codes.f: Move the aggregate to HAVING or use a subquery.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE SAL > AVG(SAL);

codes.d: The column is identified more than once in the INSERT, UPDATE, or SET transition variable.
codes.a: Column listed twice in INSERT column list or UPDATE SET.
codes.f: Remove the duplicate column reference.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(EMPNO, EMPNO) VALUES (10, 10);

codes.t: COLUMN OR EXPRESSION IN SELECT NOT IN GROUP BY
codes.d: A SELECT list with no GROUP BY contains a column outside an aggregate, or includes a non-grouped column.
codes.a: Non-aggregated column appears in SELECT when other columns are aggregated or in GROUP BY.
codes.f: Add the column to GROUP BY, or wrap it in MAX/MIN/etc.
codes.x: SELECT DEPT, NAME, SUM(SAL) FROM EMP GROUP BY DEPT;

codes.t: PARAMETER VALUE NOT VALID FOR ARG OF FUNCTION
codes.d: The value of the parameter in the indicated position must be a constant or keyword.
codes.a: Function argument that requires a literal was passed an expression or host variable.
codes.f: Pass a constant in that position.
codes.x: SUBSTR(NAME, :START, :LEN)  /* might need literal length per platform */

codes.t: ORDER BY INTEGER IS OUT OF RANGE
codes.d: An integer in the ORDER BY clause does not identify a column of the result.
codes.a: ORDER BY n where n is larger than the number of columns in the SELECT list.
codes.f: Use a valid column ordinal or column name.
codes.x: SELECT EMPNO, NAME FROM EMP ORDER BY 3;

codes.t: SELECT WITH UPDATE CONTAINS ORDER BY
codes.d: The SELECT statement contains both ORDER BY and an UPDATE clause.
codes.a: Updatable cursor declared with ORDER BY (older DB2 versions).
codes.f: Remove ORDER BY or remove FOR UPDATE OF. Use a separate fetch+update pattern.
codes.x: DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR SELECT * FROM EMP ORDER BY EMPNO FOR UPDATE OF SAL;

codes.t: DISTINCT IS SPECIFIED MORE THAN ONCE
codes.d: DISTINCT was specified twice in the same subselect.
codes.a: Two DISTINCT keywords in one SELECT.
codes.f: Keep only one DISTINCT.
codes.x: SELECT DISTINCT DISTINCT NAME FROM EMP;

codes.t: INVALID USE OF NULL IN PREDICATE
codes.d: Invalid use of NULL in a predicate (e.g., =NULL).
codes.a: Used NULL with =, <>, < etc. instead of IS NULL / IS NOT NULL.
codes.f: Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE MGR = NULL;

codes.t: STATEMENT CONTAINS TOO MANY TABLE NAMES
codes.d: The statement contains too many table names (maximum is 225).
codes.a: More than 225 tables referenced in a single query.
codes.f: Split the query into smaller joins using temp tables or views.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM T1, T2, ..., T230;

codes.d: The ESCAPE clause consists of more than one character, or the LIKE pattern is invalid.
codes.a: ESCAPE clause has multi-character value, or escape used incorrectly in LIKE pattern.
codes.f: Use a single-character escape and ensure the pattern uses the escape correctly.
codes.x: WHERE NAME LIKE 'A!%B' ESCAPE '!!'

codes.d: Statement with LIKE predicate has incompatible data types.
codes.a: LIKE used with numeric or wrong-type operand.
codes.f: Cast operands to a character type before using LIKE.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE EMPNO LIKE '1%';  /* EMPNO is INTEGER */

codes.d: LIKE predicate is invalid because the operand is not a string.
codes.a: LIKE applied to non-string column or expression.
codes.f: Use CAST(col AS CHAR) on the operand or rewrite the predicate.
codes.x: WHERE SALARY LIKE '5%'

codes.d: Correlated column reference in a subquery is not allowed in this context.
codes.a: Aggregate of a correlated column used where DB2 disallows it.
codes.f: Restructure as a join or use a CTE.
codes.x: SELECT (SELECT SUM(E.SAL) FROM EMP E2) FROM EMP E;

codes.t: IMPROPER USE OF LONG STRING COLUMN
codes.d: An LOB or LONG VARCHAR cannot be used in this context (e.g., GROUP BY, DISTINCT, ORDER BY).
codes.a: LONG VARCHAR/CLOB referenced where DB2 does not support it.
codes.f: SUBSTR or CAST the column to VARCHAR(n) before using it that way.
codes.x: SELECT DISTINCT BIO FROM EMP;  /* BIO is CLOB */

codes.t: UPDATE OR INSERT NEEDS A LONG VARCHAR VALUE
codes.d: INSERT or UPDATE missing required value for a NOT NULL LONG VARCHAR column.
codes.a: NULL provided (explicitly or by default) to NOT NULL LONG VARCHAR.
codes.f: Provide a valid value or alter the column to allow NULL.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(EMPNO) VALUES (10);  /* NOTES LONG VARCHAR NOT NULL */

codes.t: SORT FAILED, SORT KEY TOO LONG
codes.d: Sort cannot be executed because the sort key length is greater than 4000 bytes.
codes.a: ORDER BY / GROUP BY / DISTINCT keys exceed 4000 byte combined sort key length.
codes.f: Reduce the number/size of columns in the key, or hash-based aggregation.
codes.x: ORDER BY COL_4001_BYTES_TOTAL;

codes.d: The result of concatenation is more than the maximum allowed length.
codes.a: String CONCAT result exceeds 32704 bytes (32740 for graphic).
codes.f: Use CLOB or split the value across multiple columns/rows.
codes.x: SELECT C1 || C2 FROM T;   /* both VARCHAR(20000) */

codes.t: SECOND OR THIRD ARG OF SUBSTR OUT OF RANGE
codes.d: The second or third argument of the SUBSTR function is out of range.
codes.a: Start position <=0 or start+length > string length.
codes.f: Validate start and length; use LENGTH(col) to constrain arguments.
codes.x: SUBSTR(NAME, 0, 5)

codes.d: Redundant clause in ALTER statement.
codes.a: ALTER specified the same option twice.
codes.f: Remove duplicate clause.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE T ALTER COL C1 SET DATA TYPE INT SET DATA TYPE INT;

codes.d: Fetch orientation is invalid for this cursor.
codes.a: Using BEFORE/AFTER/RELATIVE on a forward-only cursor.
codes.f: Declare the cursor as SCROLL.
codes.x: FETCH PRIOR FROM C1 INTO :V;  /* C1 not SCROLL */

codes.d: The section number provided is invalid for the package.
codes.a: Plan/package corruption or wrong load module/DBRM combination.
codes.f: Rebind the package and re-link the program.
codes.x: Run-time module mismatch between DBRM and plan.

codes.t: INVALID UPDATE FOR A POSITIONED CURSOR
codes.d: Update statement is not valid because the table or view is not identified in the cursor declaration.
codes.a: UPDATE WHERE CURRENT OF references a column not specified in FOR UPDATE OF list.
codes.f: Add column to FOR UPDATE OF clause in the DECLARE CURSOR.
codes.x:
DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR SELECT * FROM EMP FOR UPDATE OF NAME;
UPDATE EMP SET SAL=99 WHERE CURRENT OF C1;

codes.d: The view named in the INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE is not defined to allow the requested operation.
codes.a: View uses DISTINCT, GROUP BY, JOIN, aggregates, or UNION — not updatable.
codes.f: Update the underlying table directly or use an INSTEAD OF trigger.
codes.x: UPDATE V_DEPT_SUMMARY SET TOTAL = 100;  /* aggregate view */

codes.d: The UPDATE statement attempted to update a column that cannot be updated.
codes.a: Column is generated, identity GENERATED ALWAYS, ROWID, or read-only catalog column.
codes.f: Remove that column from SET, or alter the column to GENERATED BY DEFAULT.
codes.x: UPDATE EMP SET EMPID = 1;  /* EMPID GENERATED ALWAYS */

codes.d: View definition contains a column without a name or a duplicate column name.
codes.a: Expressions in CREATE VIEW select list lack column aliases.
codes.f: Add column aliases or use the optional column name list in CREATE VIEW.
codes.x: CREATE VIEW V AS SELECT NAME, SAL*12 FROM EMP;

codes.t: TRIGGER TRANSITION TABLE CANNOT BE MODIFIED
codes.d: A trigger transition table cannot be modified by the trigger body.
codes.a: Trigger SQL tried to INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on OLD_TABLE or NEW_TABLE.
codes.f: Read transition tables only; perform writes on real tables.
codes.x: INSERT INTO NEW_TABLE VALUES (...);

codes.t: STATEMENT NOT ALLOWED ON A VIEW
codes.d: The statement does not identify a table.
codes.a: DROP TABLE / ALTER TABLE / LOCK TABLE invoked against a view.
codes.f: Use DROP VIEW or operate on the underlying base table.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE V_EMP ADD COL X INT;  /* V_EMP is a view */

codes.t: ONLY A TABLE NAME IS ALLOWED IN A FOREIGN KEY CLAUSE
codes.d: The object named in FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES is not a table.
codes.a: REFERENCES clause pointing to a view, synonym, or alias.
codes.f: Point the FK to the base table.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD FOREIGN KEY (DEPT) REFERENCES V_DEPT;

codes.d: The number of columns specified for the view is not the same as the number of columns of the SELECT.
codes.a: CREATE VIEW V(a,b) AS SELECT x FROM t — column count mismatch.
codes.f: Match the count, or omit the column list and use unique alias names.
codes.x: CREATE VIEW V(A,B,C) AS SELECT EMPNO, NAME FROM EMP;

codes.d: DROP or COMMENT identifies an object of the wrong type.
codes.a: DROP TABLE used on a view or alias, etc.
codes.f: Use the matching DROP statement type for the object.
codes.x: DROP TABLE V_EMP;  /* V_EMP is a view */

codes.d: WITH CHECK OPTION cannot be used because the view is not updatable, or contains unions/aggregates.
codes.a: WITH CHECK OPTION applied to non-updatable view.
codes.f: Remove WITH CHECK OPTION or redesign the view to be updatable.
codes.x: CREATE VIEW V AS SELECT DEPT, COUNT(*) FROM EMP GROUP BY DEPT WITH CHECK OPTION;

codes.t: INSERT/UPDATE CONFLICTS WITH WITH CHECK OPTION
codes.d: Insert or update would produce a row that does not conform to view definition.
codes.a: INSERT/UPDATE through a view violates the view's WHERE filter.
codes.f: Adjust values to satisfy the view definition, or update the base table.
codes.x: INSERT INTO V_DEPT_A VALUES ('B00', ...);  /* view defined WHERE DEPT='A00' */

codes.t: TABLE SPACE PLACED IN CHECK PENDING
codes.d: The table space named has been placed in check pending state.
codes.a: ALTER added a check constraint with NOT ENFORCED status, or LOAD didn't enforce constraints.
codes.f: Run CHECK DATA utility to resolve pending state.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD CONSTRAINT C1 CHECK (SAL>0) NOT ENFORCED;

codes.d: An EXPLAIN statement is not valid.
codes.a: EXPLAIN used incorrectly or PLAN_TABLE not properly defined.
codes.f: Verify PLAN_TABLE exists with correct format. Re-check EXPLAIN syntax.
codes.x: EXPLAIN ALL FOR SELECT * FROM EMP;  /* missing SET QUERYNO */

codes.t: NOT AUTHORIZED TO CREATE VIEW WITH QUALIFIER
codes.d: User does not have the privilege to create a view with the specified qualifier.
codes.a: Trying to CREATE VIEW under a schema you don't own without DBADM/SYSADM.
codes.f: Use your own schema or have SYSADM grant CREATEIN privilege.
codes.x: CREATE VIEW OTHER.V AS SELECT * FROM EMP;

codes.d: The number of arguments specified for the function is incorrect.
codes.a: Built-in or user-defined function called with wrong arg count.
codes.f: Check the function signature in DB2 SQL Reference and supply correct number of args.
codes.x: SUBSTR(NAME);  /* needs at least 2 args */

codes.d: The data type, length, or value of the argument is invalid.
codes.a: Function argument has incompatible type (e.g., LENGTH of integer).
codes.f: CAST argument to expected type or pass correct type.
codes.x: LENGTH(SALARY)

codes.d: The function or procedure name is not in the standard catalog.
codes.a: Misspelled built-in or unregistered UDF.
codes.f: Check function name spelling and ensure UDF is created/granted.
codes.x: SELECT UCASEE(NAME) FROM EMP;

codes.d: The string representation of a datetime value is incorrect.
codes.a: Bad format like '2024-13-40' or wrong delimiter.
codes.f: Format value per DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP rules, or use TO_DATE / specific format.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(HIREDATE) VALUES ('2024-13-40');

codes.t: STRING NOT A VALID DATETIME VALUE
codes.d: Value of a string representation of a datetime is not in a valid datetime format.
codes.a: Format doesn't match any of ISO, USA, EUR, JIS, LOCAL.
codes.f: Use 'YYYY-MM-DD' ISO format or set CURRENT DATE FORMAT to match.
codes.x: WHERE HIREDATE > '13/40/2024';

codes.d: An arithmetic expression contains incompatible types or invalid datetime arithmetic.
codes.a: Mixing DATE + DATE or DATE * 2, or other invalid datetime arithmetic.
codes.f: Use date arithmetic with labeled durations (e.g., DATE + 1 DAY).
codes.x: SELECT HIREDATE + HIREDATE FROM EMP;

codes.t: ARITHMETIC ON DATE/TIME OUT OF RANGE
codes.d: Result of date or time arithmetic is not within the valid range.
codes.a: Adding duration produces a value before 0001-01-01 or after 9999-12-31.
codes.f: Validate inputs and check bounds before computation.
codes.x: SELECT DATE('9999-12-31') + 1 YEAR FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.d: The local date format exit routine has not been installed.
codes.a: DSNHDECP set LOCAL format but DSNXVDTX/DSNXVTMX missing.
codes.f: Install the local date/time exit routine, or change DSNHDECP to ISO/USA/etc.
codes.x: SELECT DATE(:H) FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.d: Local date/time length has been increased and program needs to be rebuilt.
codes.a: DSNHDECP local length changed; program compiled with old length.
codes.f: Recompile and rebind all programs using local date/time format.
codes.x: Re-precompile with new DSNHDECP.

codes.t: REFERENCE TO A CURRENT DATE/TIME SPECIAL REGISTER INVALID
codes.d: MVS time-of-day clock value is invalid.
codes.a: TOD clock issue when CURRENT TIMESTAMP referenced.
codes.f: Operator must verify system clock; contact systems programmer.
codes.x: SELECT CURRENT TIMESTAMP FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.d: The string representation of a name is not valid.
codes.a: Identifier string passed to a function (e.g., RID, IDENTITY_VAL_LOCAL) is invalid.
codes.f: Pass a valid identifier conforming to SQL naming rules.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM TABLE(RID(:NM));

codes.d: CCSID value not valid or not supported.
codes.a: Specified CCSID is not installed or invalid.
codes.f: Use a supported CCSID. Check installed CCSIDs in DSNHDECP.
codes.x: CAST(NAME AS CHAR(10) CCSID 9999);

codes.t: ALTER TABLE COLUMN TYPE CHANGE INVALID
codes.d: The attributes specified for the column are inconsistent with the existing column.
codes.a: ALTER COLUMN tries to shorten length, change incompatible type, or reduce precision.
codes.f: Only widen length/precision, or recreate the table.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ALTER COLUMN NAME SET DATA TYPE CHAR(5);  /* was CHAR(20) */

codes.d: A string of mixed SBCS and DBCS data is not properly formed.
codes.a: Missing or unbalanced shift-out / shift-in (0x0E / 0x0F) bytes.
codes.f: Validate mixed data formation. Use CAST and verify CCSID.
codes.x: INSERT INTO T VALUES (X'0E41');  /* missing shift-in */

codes.d: Qualified column name not allowed in ORDER BY when the query contains a set operator.
codes.a: ORDER BY T.col on UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT — must use column number or alias.
codes.f: Use ordinal positions or unqualified column names in ORDER BY.
codes.x: SELECT NAME FROM EMP UNION SELECT NAME FROM CONS ORDER BY EMP.NAME;

codes.t: PREPARE STATEMENT IS BLANK OR EMPTY
codes.d: The operand of PREPARE or EXECUTE IMMEDIATE is blank or empty.
codes.a: Host variable passed to PREPARE contains only blanks or empty string.
codes.f: Validate the SQL text is non-empty before PREPARE.
codes.x:
MOVE SPACES TO SQL-TEXT.
EXEC SQL PREPARE S FROM :SQL-TEXT END-EXEC.

codes.d: Illegal use of keyword. Token expected was a different list of tokens.
codes.a: Reserved word used as identifier without delimiter.
codes.f: Rename or delimit identifier with double quotes (delimited identifier).
codes.x: CREATE TABLE ORDER (C1 INT);

codes.d: The identified object is undefined in the DB2 subsystem.
codes.a: Misspelled name, wrong qualifier/schema, or object not yet created.
codes.f: Verify name and qualifier; check CURRENT SCHEMA and CURRENT PATH.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM EMPLYEE;  /* misspelled */

codes.d: The column is not in the table specified.
codes.a: Misspelled column or wrong table referenced.
codes.f: Check column spelling and the SELECT/FROM table list.
codes.x: SELECT EMPNAME FROM EMP;  /* column is NAME */

codes.t: COLUMN NOT IN ANY TABLE OF FROM CLAUSE
codes.d: The column does not exist in any table or view identified in the FROM clause.
codes.a: Column referenced in SELECT, WHERE, ON, etc. doesn't exist in any FROM table.
codes.f: Qualify the column or correct the spelling/name.
codes.x: SELECT EMP.SALARY FROM DEPT;

codes.t: ORDER BY COLUMN NOT IN RESULT TABLE
codes.d: ORDER BY references a column that is not part of the result table.
codes.a: Tried ORDER BY on a column not in SELECT list (in some DB2 modes).
codes.f: Add the column to SELECT list or use a column expression already in the list.
codes.x: SELECT EMPNO FROM EMP ORDER BY SALARY;  /* SALARY not in SELECT */

codes.d: The required PLAN_TABLE does not exist.
codes.a: EXPLAIN issued without owner's PLAN_TABLE being defined.
codes.f: Create PLAN_TABLE using the install sample DSNTESC.
codes.x: EXPLAIN PLAN FOR SELECT * FROM EMP;

codes.d: All output parameters in a CALL statement must be specified with a parameter marker (?) or a host variable.
codes.a: OUT or INOUT parameter passed as literal in dynamic CALL.
codes.f: Use parameter markers for OUT/INOUT parameters.
codes.x: CALL MYPROC(1, 'literal');  /* OUT param can't be literal */

codes.d: The data types of the operands for the operator are not compatible.
codes.a: Comparing/adding incompatible types like CHAR + INT.
codes.f: Convert operands with CAST to compatible types.
codes.x: WHERE EMPNO = 'A123';  /* EMPNO is INTEGER */

codes.t: AN ARITHMETIC FUNCTION OR OPERATOR IS APPLIED TO NON-NUMERIC
codes.d: Arithmetic operator or numeric function applied to a non-numeric operand.
codes.a: Adding to a CHAR column or applying ABS to a string.
codes.f: Cast to numeric type before arithmetic.
codes.x: SELECT NAME + 1 FROM EMP;

codes.d: The UPDATE or INSERT statement specifies a value that is longer than the column maximum.
codes.a: Inserting/updating a string longer than the column definition.
codes.f: Increase the column length, or truncate the input value.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(NAME) VALUES ('VERYVERYVERYLONGNAMEHERE');

codes.d: The numeric literal cannot be used as specified because it is out of range.
codes.a: Literal exceeds data type range (e.g., 9999999 into SMALLINT).
codes.f: Use a value within the column's range or alter the column.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(AGE) VALUES (99999);  /* AGE SMALLINT */

codes.d: A calculated or derived numeric value is not within the range of the data type.
codes.a: Result of arithmetic overflows the column or host var type.
codes.f: Cast operands to wider type; validate inputs.
codes.x: INSERT INTO REP(TOTAL) SELECT SUM(SAL) FROM EMP;  /* TOTAL is INT, sum overflows */

codes.t: NULL INSERT INTO NOT NULL COLUMN
codes.d: An update or insert value is null, but the object column cannot contain null values.
codes.a: Trying to assign NULL to a NOT NULL column.
codes.f: Provide a non-null value or alter the column to allow NULL/give a default.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(EMPNO, NAME) VALUES (10, NULL);

codes.d: A value is not compatible with the data type of its assignment target.
codes.a: INSERT/UPDATE value type incompatible with the column's data type.
codes.f: CAST the value or change the column type.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(HIREDATE) VALUES ('NOT A DATE');

codes.d: The operand of COUNT is invalid.
codes.a: Old DB2 syntax restriction on COUNT(DISTINCT col).
codes.f: Use COUNT(*) or COUNT(DISTINCT col) per current DB2 syntax.
codes.x: SELECT COUNT(ALL DISTINCT NAME) FROM EMP;

codes.d: The floating point literal contains more than 30 characters.
codes.f: Shorten the literal or use a host variable.
codes.x: SELECT 1.23456789012345678901234567890E5 FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.d: CURRENT SQLID cannot be used in statement.
codes.a: Special register used in a context that disallows it (e.g., check constraint).
codes.f: Remove the special register reference from that context.
codes.x: CHECK (USER_COL = CURRENT SQLID);

codes.t: SUBQUERY RETURNS MORE THAN ONE COLUMN
codes.d: The SELECT of a subquery specifies more than one column.
codes.a: Subquery used as expression returns multiple columns.
codes.f: Limit subquery to one column or use a row constructor with appropriate comparison.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM EMP WHERE EMPNO = (SELECT EMPNO, NAME FROM DEPT WHERE DEPT='A');

codes.d: Overflow occurred during numeric data type conversion.
codes.a: Implicit conversion target can't hold the value.
codes.f: Cast to a wider type or validate inputs.
codes.x: SELECT INTEGER(99999999999) FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.t: LIKE PREDICATE NOT VALID FOR THIS COLUMN
codes.d: A LIKE predicate is invalid because the first operand is not a string.
codes.a: LIKE on numeric or datetime column.
codes.f: Cast operand to CHAR/VARCHAR before LIKE.
codes.x: WHERE HIREDATE LIKE '2024%';

codes.d: Corresponding columns in operands of UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT are not compatible.
codes.a: UNION'd queries have columns of incompatible data types in the same position.
codes.f: CAST columns to a common type in both legs.
codes.x: SELECT EMPNO FROM EMP UNION SELECT NAME FROM EMP;

codes.d: An operand of UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT contains a LONG STRING column.
codes.a: Set operations don't support LONG VARCHAR/LONG VARGRAPHIC operands.
codes.f: Cast to VARCHAR(n) where n is supported.
codes.x: SELECT BIO FROM EMP UNION SELECT BIO FROM CAND;

codes.t: TWO PARAMETER MARKERS USED IN AN OPERATION
codes.d: A statement contains two parameter markers on both sides of an operator.
codes.a: Both operands of an operator are ? markers; DB2 can't determine types.
codes.f: Cast one operand: CAST(? AS INT) = ?.
codes.x: WHERE ? = ?

codes.d: A statement uses a parameter marker in an invalid context (e.g., in a select list without typing).
codes.a: Untyped parameter marker where DB2 cannot infer type.
codes.f: Use CAST(? AS type) to provide explicit type information.
codes.x: SELECT ? FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.d: Decimal division is invalid because the result would have a negative scale.
codes.a: Division produces a scale that exceeds limits.
codes.f: Cast operands to a smaller precision or use floating point.
codes.x: SELECT DEC(1,31,31)/DEC(1,31,31) FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.d: The value of a character string argument is not in the expected format.
codes.a: Casting a string with non-numeric characters to a numeric type.
codes.f: Validate or sanitize the string before CAST.
codes.x: SELECT INTEGER('12A3') FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.d: Operands of UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT do not have the same number of columns.
codes.a: Differing number of columns in SELECT clauses joined by UNION.
codes.f: Make column counts match in each leg of the set operation.
codes.x: SELECT EMPNO, NAME FROM EMP UNION SELECT EMPNO FROM CAND;

codes.t: CURSOR NOT OPEN ON FETCH OR CLOSE
codes.d: The cursor identified in a FETCH or CLOSE statement is not open.
codes.a: FETCH/CLOSE issued before OPEN, or after a ROLLBACK closed the cursor.
codes.f: OPEN the cursor before FETCH/CLOSE. Use WITH HOLD if you need persistence across COMMIT.
codes.x: EXEC SQL CLOSE C1 END-EXEC.  /* never opened */

codes.d: An OPEN was issued for a cursor that is already open.
codes.a: OPEN issued twice on the same cursor without an intervening CLOSE.
codes.f: CLOSE before re-OPENing, or skip the second OPEN.
codes.x:
EXEC SQL OPEN C1 END-EXEC.
EXEC SQL OPEN C1 END-EXEC.

codes.d: A column cannot be updated because it is not identified in the FOR UPDATE OF clause.
codes.a: Positioned UPDATE setting a column not listed in FOR UPDATE OF.
codes.f: Add column to FOR UPDATE OF list in DECLARE CURSOR, or rebind with proper option.
codes.x:
DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR SELECT * FROM EMP FOR UPDATE OF NAME;
UPDATE EMP SET SALARY = 100 WHERE CURRENT OF C1;

codes.d: The cursor name is not defined.
codes.a: Referenced cursor name was never declared.
codes.f: Add DECLARE CURSOR before its first use.
codes.x: OPEN C_UNKNOWN;

codes.d: The cursor specified in an UPDATE or DELETE WHERE CURRENT OF is not open.
codes.a: Positioned UPDATE/DELETE issued before OPEN, or after COMMIT closed cursor.
codes.f: OPEN cursor first; declare WITH HOLD if needed across COMMIT.
codes.x: UPDATE EMP SET SAL=100 WHERE CURRENT OF C1;  /* C1 not open */

codes.t: CURSOR NOT POSITIONED ON A ROW
codes.d: The cursor for UPDATE/DELETE WHERE CURRENT OF is not positioned on a row.
codes.a: FETCH returned +100 (no row) or no fetch issued yet.
codes.f: Check SQLCODE after each FETCH. Only issue positioned UPDATE/DELETE after successful FETCH.
codes.x:
FETCH C1 INTO :V;  /* returns +100 */
DELETE WHERE CURRENT OF C1;

codes.t: TABLE NAMED IS NOT THE TABLE OF CURSOR
codes.d: The table named in UPDATE/DELETE WHERE CURRENT OF is not the table of the cursor.
codes.a: Positioned UPDATE references a different table than the cursor selects from.
codes.f: Make the UPDATE/DELETE table match the cursor's table.
codes.x:
DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR SELECT * FROM EMP;
DELETE FROM DEPT WHERE CURRENT OF C1;

codes.t: UPDATE/DELETE NOT ALLOWED ON THIS CURSOR
codes.d: The table or view specified in the cursor cannot be modified.
codes.a: Cursor is read-only (SELECT with aggregates, joins, etc.).
codes.f: Restructure the cursor query or use a different update path.
codes.x:
DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR SELECT DEPT, AVG(SAL) FROM EMP GROUP BY DEPT;
UPDATE EMP SET SAL=100 WHERE CURRENT OF C1;

codes.d: FOR UPDATE clause specified for a cursor that cannot be updated.
codes.a: FOR UPDATE OF on a read-only result (joins, set ops, aggregates, DISTINCT).
codes.f: Remove FOR UPDATE OF or rewrite the cursor as updatable.
codes.x: DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR SELECT DEPT, SUM(SAL) FROM EMP GROUP BY DEPT FOR UPDATE OF DEPT;

codes.d: Statement reference to remote object is invalid.
codes.a: DDL or statement type doesn't allow three-part-name remote reference.
codes.f: Use CONNECT TO LOC and refer to objects locally.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE REMOTE.SCHEMA.NEWT (C1 INT);

codes.t: ALIAS MUST NOT BE DEFINED ON ANOTHER LOCAL ALIAS
codes.d: ALIAS cannot point to another local alias.
codes.a: CREATE ALIAS A FOR B where B is also a local alias.
codes.f: Point alias to the base table or to a remote object.
codes.x: CREATE ALIAS A1 FOR LOCAL.A2;  /* A2 is local alias */

codes.t: CURSOR IS NOT IN A PREPARED STATE
codes.d: Dynamic cursor refers to a statement that is not in a prepared state.
codes.a: OPEN cursor before its PREPARE has been executed.
codes.f: Issue PREPARE before OPEN. Check if commit invalidated the prepared statement.
codes.x:
DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR S1;
OPEN C1;  /* S1 not yet PREPAREd */

codes.t: DESCRIBE NOT EXECUTED ON A PREPARED STATEMENT
codes.d: DESCRIBE statement does not identify a prepared statement.
codes.a: DESCRIBE issued for a statement that wasn't PREPAREd in this thread.
codes.f: Run PREPARE before DESCRIBE.
codes.x: DESCRIBE S1 INTO :SQLDA;  /* never PREPAREd */

codes.d: Cursor has not been assigned a result set.
codes.a: Cursor was declared but never associated with a statement before OPEN.
codes.f: Use DECLARE cursor FOR statement-name, then PREPARE & OPEN.
codes.x: DECLARE C1 CURSOR;  OPEN C1;

codes.d: The statement named in EXECUTE is not a prepared SQL statement.
codes.a: EXECUTE on a name that wasn't PREPAREd, or that points to a cursor.
codes.f: PREPARE the statement first. Do not EXECUTE cursor names.
codes.x: EXECUTE S1;  /* S1 not PREPAREd */

codes.t: PREPARE STATEMENT IDENTIFIES OPEN CURSOR STATEMENT
codes.d: Cannot PREPARE the statement that is the SELECT statement of an open cursor.
codes.a: PREPARE attempted while a cursor based on the same statement is open.
codes.f: CLOSE the cursor first, then PREPARE.
codes.x: OPEN C1; PREPARE S1 FROM :SQL;  /* C1 based on S1 */

codes.t: STATEMENT IN ERROR STATE AT BIND
codes.d: SQL statement cannot be executed because it was in error at bind time.
codes.a: Bind-time error wasn't resolved; package contains a non-executable section.
codes.f: Fix the SQL error and REBIND the package.
codes.x: Package contains a SELECT that references a missing table at BIND; running it fails -525.

codes.d: The insert or update value of foreign key is not equal to any value of the parent key.
codes.a: Inserted/updated value doesn't exist in the referenced parent table.
codes.f: Ensure parent key row exists, or change FK value.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(DEPT) VALUES ('Z99');  /* Z99 not in DEPT */

codes.d: The update of a parent key would render rows in the dependent table unrelated.
codes.a: UPDATE on parent key with NO ACTION/RESTRICT delete rule has dependents.
codes.f: Delete or update dependent rows first, or change to CASCADE.
codes.x: UPDATE DEPT SET DEPTNO='X99' WHERE DEPTNO='A00';  /* EMP rows depend on A00 */

codes.d: DELETE violates a referential constraint with delete rule RESTRICT or NO ACTION.
codes.a: Parent row delete blocked by dependent rows.
codes.f: Delete child rows first or change FK rule to CASCADE/SET NULL.
codes.x: DELETE FROM DEPT WHERE DEPTNO='A00';

codes.d: An INSERT involving a subquery and the same table has more than one row in result.
codes.a: INSERT ... SELECT into table referenced by subquery returning multiple rows.
codes.f: Restrict the subquery to a single row or use a temporary table.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP_BACKUP SELECT * FROM EMP;  /* recursive self-reference */

codes.d: The primary key cannot be updated to a value that is null or duplicates an existing key.
codes.a: UPDATE on PK violates unique constraint.
codes.f: Use a non-duplicate PK value or delete-and-reinsert.
codes.x: UPDATE EMP SET EMPNO=100 WHERE EMPNO=200;  /* 100 already exists */

codes.t: RESULT OF UPDATE OR DELETE WOULD BE INDETERMINATE
codes.d: The result of an UPDATE or DELETE cannot be predictable due to a self-referencing constraint.
codes.a: Update/Delete on a table with a self-referencing FK could affect rows non-deterministically.
codes.f: Restructure the update or break it into steps.
codes.x: UPDATE EMP SET MGR_ID=5 WHERE MGR_ID IN (SELECT EMPNO FROM EMP WHERE ...);

codes.t: DELETE NOT VALID DUE TO REFERENTIAL CONSTRAINTS
codes.d: DELETE not allowed because the table is involved in a referential constraint.
codes.a: Table is a parent in a constraint that prevents the DELETE operation.
codes.f: Adjust referential rules or delete dependents first.
codes.x: DELETE FROM DEPT;  /* EMP has FK to DEPT */

codes.d: The same column is identified more than once in a PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY clause.
codes.a: Same column listed twice in PK or FK column list.
codes.f: Remove duplicate columns.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD CONSTRAINT FK1 FOREIGN KEY (DEPT, DEPT) REFERENCES DEPT;

codes.t: FOREIGN KEY DOES NOT CONFORM TO PARENT KEY
codes.d: Foreign key column count or data types do not match the parent key.
codes.a: FK column types/lengths don't match referenced PK.
codes.f: Make FK columns same type/length as PK columns.
codes.x: FOREIGN KEY (DEPTNO CHAR(2)) REFERENCES DEPT(DEPTNO CHAR(3));

codes.t: NO PRIMARY KEY EXISTS ON PARENT TABLE
codes.d: The named table cannot be the parent table because it does not have a primary key.
codes.a: FK references a table without a PK or matching unique key.
codes.f: Add a primary key to the parent table.
codes.x: FOREIGN KEY (DEPT) REFERENCES DEPT_NO_PK;

codes.d: Table definition is incomplete because it lacks a primary index or required ROWID column.
codes.a: Trying to INSERT into a table where required catalog setup is incomplete.
codes.f: Create a primary index on the PK or add the missing structural element.
codes.x: INSERT INTO T1 VALUES (...);  /* T1 created without PK index */

codes.t: COLUMN IDENTIFIED IN A PRIMARY KEY CANNOT BE NULLABLE
codes.d: A nullable column cannot be in a PRIMARY KEY constraint.
codes.a: Column declared as nullable used in PRIMARY KEY.
codes.f: ALTER COLUMN to NOT NULL or remove from PK.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T (C1 INT, PRIMARY KEY (C1));  /* C1 nullable */

codes.t: DELETE OR UPDATE INVALIDATES A CHECK CONSTRAINT
codes.d: Row in parent table cannot be deleted because the check constraint restricts the deletion.
codes.a: Operation would cause the table to violate a CHECK constraint.
codes.f: Loosen the constraint or change the data being modified.
codes.x: UPDATE EMP SET SAL=-1;  /* CHECK (SAL>0) */

codes.t: CHECK CONSTRAINT CANNOT BE ADDED, TABLE CONTAINS A ROW THAT VIOLATES
codes.d: An attempt to add a check constraint failed because the table contains rows that violate it.
codes.a: Existing data fails the new constraint condition.
codes.f: Clean up data first, or use NOT ENFORCED while you fix, then turn back on.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD CONSTRAINT C1 CHECK (SAL>0);

codes.d: The requested operation is not allowed because a row does not satisfy a check constraint.
codes.a: INSERT/UPDATE violates CHECK constraint.
codes.f: Adjust input data to satisfy the constraint.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP(SAL) VALUES (-100);  /* CHECK (SAL>=0) */

codes.d: The check constraint is invalid because the constraint references something disallowed.
codes.a: CHECK references a UDF, host variable, or subquery — not allowed.
codes.f: Use only deterministic column references and built-in functions in CHECK.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD CHECK (SAL < (SELECT MAX(SAL) FROM MGR));

codes.t: CHECK CONSTRAINT DEFINED WITH AN INVALID COLUMN
codes.d: The check constraint is invalid because the column is invalid for use in a constraint.
codes.a: CHECK references a non-existent or invalid column (e.g., generated, LOB).
codes.f: Reference only valid base columns.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD CHECK (NOTES > 'A');  /* NOTES is CLOB */

codes.t: STATEMENT NOT ALLOWED BECAUSE PLAN OR PACKAGE IS DYNAMICRULES BIND
codes.d: The dynamic SQL statement is disallowed because of the DYNAMICRULES option.
codes.a: DYNAMICRULES BIND prohibits certain dynamic SQL types.
codes.f: Rebind with DYNAMICRULES RUN or convert to static SQL.
codes.x: Bind plan with DYNAMICRULES(BIND); attempt dynamic CREATE TABLE.

codes.d: The authorization ID does not have the privilege to perform operation on object.
codes.a: User lacks GRANT for the operation (SELECT, UPDATE, etc.) on the object.
codes.f: GRANT the required privilege or use a different auth ID.
codes.x: SELECT * FROM HR.SALARY;  /* user not granted SELECT */

codes.d: The authorization ID does not have the privilege to perform the operation.
codes.a: Operation requires admin authority (SYSADM, DBADM) that user does not hold.
codes.f: Grant SYSADM/DBADM or have admin perform the operation.
codes.x: CREATE TABLESPACE TS1 IN DB1;  /* user not DBADM */

codes.t: SCHEMA NAME OR QUALIFIER NOT VALID
codes.d: The auth ID is not authorized to specify the specified schema as the qualifier.
codes.a: CURRENT SQLID set to a value the user is not authorized to use.
codes.f: SET CURRENT SQLID to your own ID or one you have SYSADM rights for.
codes.x: SET CURRENT SQLID = 'OTHER';

codes.t: AN AUTH ID CANNOT GRANT TO ITSELF
codes.d: An authorization ID cannot grant a privilege to itself.
codes.a: GRANT statement attempts to grant to the current SQLID.
codes.f: Grant to a different auth ID; you already implicitly have it.
codes.x: GRANT SELECT ON EMP TO USER1;  /* CURRENT SQLID is USER1 */

codes.t: AN AUTH ID CANNOT REVOKE FROM ITSELF
codes.d: An authorization ID cannot revoke a privilege from itself.
codes.a: REVOKE issued targeting the current SQLID.
codes.f: Have another auth ID with admin authority perform the revoke.
codes.x: REVOKE SELECT ON EMP FROM USER1;  /* CURRENT SQLID is USER1 */

codes.d: REVOKE cannot be executed because the auth ID does not have the privilege specified.
codes.a: Trying to REVOKE a privilege you didn't GRANT, or didn't hold WITH GRANT OPTION.
codes.f: Use proper auth ID that originally granted, or have admin do the revoke.
codes.x: REVOKE SELECT ON EMP FROM OTHER;  /* you didn't grant it */

codes.d: Inconsistent or invalid combination of options specified in a GRANT.
codes.a: Conflicting privileges or invalid syntax in GRANT.
codes.f: Correct GRANT syntax per SQL Reference.
codes.x: GRANT SELECT, ALL ON EMP TO USER1;

codes.t: REVOKE INVALID BECAUSE OF PRIOR GRANT
codes.d: The revoke is invalid because the auth ID was granted the privilege with GRANT OPTION.
codes.a: Trying to REVOKE privileges in a way that violates DB2 grant semantics.
codes.f: REVOKE WITH GRANT OPTION first, then revoke privilege.
codes.x: REVOKE SELECT ON EMP FROM USER1;  /* USER1 has WITH GRANT OPTION */

codes.d: GRANT or REVOKE not allowed because DB2 was started with authorization functions disabled.
codes.a: DB2 install set NO AUTH; security checking disabled.
codes.f: Restart DB2 with authorization enabled.
codes.x: GRANT SELECT ON EMP TO USER1;

codes.t: OPERATION NOT ALLOWED ON CATALOG TABLE
codes.d: Operation is not allowed on a DB2 catalog table.
codes.a: Attempt to UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT/ALTER catalog (SYSIBM.*) tables.
codes.f: Use approved DB2 commands (e.g., DDL) instead of direct catalog updates.
codes.x: DELETE FROM SYSIBM.SYSTABLES WHERE NAME='EMP';

codes.d: Authorization ID specification is invalid.
codes.a: Invalid character or length in SET CURRENT SQLID or similar.
codes.f: Use valid auth ID (1-8 chars EBCDIC).
codes.x: SET CURRENT SQLID = 'TOOLONGAUTHID';

codes.d: The statement would result in a multi-site update where DB2 does not support it.
codes.a: Two-phase commit not configured but transaction spans multiple sites.
codes.f: Configure DDF for two-phase commit, or restructure to update at one site.
codes.x: INSERT INTO REMOTE1.T VALUES (...); UPDATE REMOTE2.T ...;

codes.t: RESULT EXPRESSIONS OF CASE CANNOT ALL BE NULL
codes.d: The result expressions of a CASE expression cannot all be NULL.
codes.a: Every WHEN clause returns NULL, so DB2 can't determine result type.
codes.f: CAST at least one result to a specific type.
codes.x: CASE WHEN X=1 THEN NULL ELSE NULL END

codes.t: DATA TYPES OF CASE EXPRESSION ARE NOT COMPATIBLE
codes.d: The result expressions of a CASE expression are not compatible.
codes.a: Different branches of CASE return incompatible types.
codes.f: CAST results to a common type.
codes.x: CASE WHEN A=1 THEN NAME ELSE SALARY END

codes.t: SEARCH CONDITION IN CASE NOT BOOLEAN
codes.d: Search condition in a SEARCHED-WHEN clause of CASE is not boolean.
codes.a: Non-boolean expression used after WHEN.
codes.f: Use a proper comparison or predicate.
codes.x: CASE WHEN NAME THEN 1 ELSE 0 END

codes.t: INVALID USE OF NULL OR DEFAULT
codes.d: Invalid use of NULL or DEFAULT keyword in a context where they are not allowed.
codes.a: NULL or DEFAULT used in an expression where DB2 can't process it.
codes.f: Replace with explicit values or use CAST(NULL AS type).
codes.x: SELECT NULL + 1 FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1;

codes.t: DUPLICATE SCHEMA NAME IN CURRENT PATH
codes.d: The schema name appears more than once in the SQL PATH register.
codes.a: SET CURRENT PATH had duplicates.
codes.f: Remove duplicates from path.
codes.x: SET CURRENT PATH = 'SYSIBM', 'A', 'A';

codes.d: The total length of the SQL PATH is too long.
codes.a: SET CURRENT PATH exceeded 2048 bytes total.
codes.f: Reduce number/length of schemas in path.
codes.x: SET CURRENT PATH = 'S1', 'S2', ..., 'S200';

codes.d: An attempt was made to create a table or index that already exists.
codes.a: Object already exists in the schema.
codes.f: Use CREATE OR REPLACE, drop and recreate, or choose a different name.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE EMP (...);  /* EMP already exists */

codes.d: The name of the object to be created is identical to the existing name of another object of the same type.
codes.a: CREATE statement conflicts with existing object.
codes.f: Choose a different name or drop existing object.
codes.x: CREATE INDEX IX_EMP ON EMP(EMPNO);  /* IX_EMP exists */

codes.t: TOO MANY COLUMNS IN INDEX KEY
codes.d: Too many columns specified in a CREATE INDEX statement.
codes.a: Index key has more columns than DB2 limit (64).
codes.f: Reduce key columns. Consider composite key or different index strategy.
codes.x: CREATE INDEX IX1 ON T(C1, C2, ..., C65);

codes.d: A unique index cannot be created because the table contains duplicates of the proposed key.
codes.a: Existing data has duplicates that would violate uniqueness.
codes.f: Find duplicates with GROUP BY HAVING COUNT(*)>1 and resolve before creating index.
codes.x: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IX_NAME ON EMP(NAME);  /* dupes exist */

codes.d: A length, precision, or scale value is invalid.
codes.a: Out-of-range values for column data type definition.
codes.f: Use valid range (e.g., DECIMAL precision 1-31, scale 0..p).
codes.x: DECIMAL(35,40)

codes.t: OPERATION NOT DEFINED FOR THIS OBJECT
codes.d: Operation is not defined for the system catalog or system table.
codes.a: Operation invalid for catalog tables, system temp tables, etc.
codes.f: Use DB2 provided commands instead of generic DDL on catalog.
codes.x: DROP TABLE SYSIBM.SYSTABLES;

codes.d: A duplicate column name was specified in CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX, or similar.
codes.a: Two columns with the same name in DDL.
codes.f: Use unique column names.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T (C1 INT, C1 INT);

codes.d: Primary or unique key columns exceed the maximum length.
codes.a: Sum of PK column lengths > 2000 bytes.
codes.f: Reduce key column lengths or use a surrogate key.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T (C1 VARCHAR(2100), PRIMARY KEY (C1));

codes.d: The index cannot be created because the sum of the column lengths exceeds the maximum.
codes.a: Combined index columns exceed page-size derived limit.
codes.f: Use larger page size, fewer columns, or shorter columns.
codes.x: CREATE INDEX IX1 ON T(C1, C2);  /* total > 2000 bytes */

codes.t: RESOURCE IN USE — CANNOT ALTER OR DROP
codes.d: DROP/ALTER cannot be processed because the resource is in use.
codes.a: Object being modified has open cursors or other access.
codes.f: Close cursors, end units of work, then retry.
codes.x: DROP TABLE EMP;  /* cursor still open */

codes.t: OBJECT CANNOT BE DROPPED BECAUSE OTHER OBJECTS DEPEND ON IT
codes.d: An object cannot be dropped because another object is dependent on it.
codes.a: DROP blocked by RI constraints, views, triggers, or other deps.
codes.f: Drop dependents first or use CASCADE option where supported.
codes.x: DROP TABLE DEPT;  /* EMP has FK to DEPT */

codes.t: OPERATION NOT ALLOWED ON CATALOG TABLE
codes.d: Operation cannot be performed on a DB2 catalog table.
codes.a: Direct UPDATE on catalog table not allowed.
codes.f: Use DB2 DDL or commands; do not directly modify catalog.
codes.x: UPDATE SYSIBM.SYSTABLES SET NAME='X' WHERE NAME='EMP';

codes.d: Operations require that DSNDB06 catalog be in special status.
codes.a: Required pending DDL on catalog while it's not in proper state.
codes.f: Coordinate with DBA; ensure catalog tablespaces are quiesced before maintenance.
codes.x: ALTER TABLESPACE DSNDB06.SYSDBASE BUFFERPOOL BP1;

codes.t: KEYWORD NOT ALLOWED FOR TABLESPACE TYPE
codes.d: The keyword is not allowed for this type of tablespace.
codes.a: CREATE/ALTER TABLESPACE used option not valid for that type (LOB, simple, etc.).
codes.f: Remove or correct the option per allowed list.
codes.x: CREATE LOB TABLESPACE TS1 SEGSIZE 4;  /* SEGSIZE not valid for LOB */

codes.d: FOR MIXED DATA is specified but installed system does not support mixed CCSID.
codes.a: DSNHDECP install lacks mixed CCSID support.
codes.f: Install mixed-data support or omit FOR MIXED DATA.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T (C1 CHAR(10) FOR MIXED DATA);

codes.d: A constraint with the same name already exists.
codes.a: CREATE/ALTER TABLE specifies an existing constraint name.
codes.f: Use a unique constraint name.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD CONSTRAINT C1 CHECK (SAL>0);  /* C1 exists */

codes.t: TABLE ALREADY HAS A PRIMARY KEY
codes.d: A table can only have one primary key.
codes.a: Trying to add a second PRIMARY KEY.
codes.f: DROP existing PK or use UNIQUE constraint instead.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD PRIMARY KEY (NAME);  /* EMPNO is PK */

codes.t: TABLE DOES NOT HAVE AN INDEX FOR THE PRIMARY KEY
codes.d: A table is defined with a primary key but does not have an index to enforce it.
codes.a: Table created without ensuring primary index exists.
codes.f: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on the PK columns.
codes.x: Table EMP with PRIMARY KEY but unique index missing.

codes.d: ALTER TABLE is not executable because the table is dependent or in another state.
codes.a: Tablespace status (e.g., REORG-pending) blocks ALTER.
codes.f: Resolve tablespace status (REORG, RECOVER) first.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD COLUMN X INT;  /* TS REORP */

codes.d: ALTER TABLESPACE not allowed because no storage attributes were defined.
codes.a: Tablespace lacks attributes for the requested ALTER.
codes.f: Specify storage attributes or drop/recreate the TS.
codes.x: ALTER TABLESPACE TS1 USING STOGROUP SG1;

codes.d: Mutually exclusive clauses specified in the same statement.
codes.a: E.g., specifying both USING STOGROUP and USING VCAT.
codes.f: Remove one of the conflicting clauses.
codes.x: CREATE TABLESPACE TS1 USING STOGROUP SG1 USING VCAT MYVCAT;

codes.t: SET NULL CANNOT APPLY TO NOT NULL COLUMN
codes.d: SET NULL delete rule cannot be used with a foreign key where the column is NOT NULL.
codes.a: FK ON DELETE SET NULL on a NOT NULL column.
codes.f: Allow nulls on the FK columns or change delete rule to CASCADE/RESTRICT.
codes.x: FOREIGN KEY (DEPT) REFERENCES DEPT ON DELETE SET NULL;  /* DEPT NOT NULL */

codes.t: WHERE NOT NULL SPECIFIED FOR NON-NULLABLE COLUMN
codes.d: WHERE NOT NULL is specified for a non-nullable column.
codes.a: Unnecessary or invalid WHERE NOT NULL on an index that doesn't support it.
codes.f: Remove WHERE NOT NULL from CREATE INDEX.
codes.x: CREATE INDEX IX1 ON T(C1) WHERE C1 IS NOT NULL;  /* C1 NOT NULL */

codes.t: FOREIGN KEY TOO LONG OR HAS TOO MANY COLUMNS
codes.d: Foreign key length or count exceeds limit.
codes.a: Composite FK exceeds DB2 limits.
codes.f: Reduce columns or lengths in FK.
codes.x: FOREIGN KEY (C1, C2, ..., C65) REFERENCES T_PARENT;

codes.t: DELETE RULE CANNOT BE NO ACTION OR CASCADE
codes.d: Table cannot be defined as a dependent of a parent table using the indicated delete rule because of conflicting rules.
codes.a: RI cycle requires consistent delete rules; specified rule conflicts.
codes.f: Adjust delete rule to be compatible with existing constraints.
codes.x: Cycle: A->B->C->A with mixed CASCADE and NO ACTION.

codes.t: DELETE RULE MUST BE CASCADE/SET NULL
codes.d: DELETE rule must be CASCADE or SET NULL because of existing relationships.
codes.a: Existing RI cycle requires specific rule.
codes.f: Change rule to match cycle constraints.
codes.x: FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE RESTRICT;  /* cycle requires CASCADE */

codes.t: DELETE RULE MUST NOT BE CASCADE
codes.d: DELETE rule cannot be CASCADE.
codes.a: Self-referencing table or cycle disallows CASCADE.
codes.f: Use RESTRICT or SET NULL.
codes.x: FOREIGN KEY (MGR_ID) REFERENCES EMP(EMPNO) ON DELETE CASCADE;  /* self-ref */

codes.t: DELETE RULES NOT THE SAME OR INVALID
codes.d: DELETE rules cannot be different or cannot be SET NULL for multiple paths.
codes.a: Multiple paths to same dependent table have inconsistent delete rules.
codes.f: Make all paths use the same delete rule.
codes.x: Two FKs to EMP from different parents with different ON DELETE.

codes.t: PARTITION KEY RANGES NOT IN ASCENDING ORDER
codes.d: Partition key ranges are not in ascending order.
codes.a: PARTITION BY RANGE values not sorted ascending.
codes.f: List ranges in ascending order.
codes.x: PARTITION BY RANGE (DT) (PART P1 VALUES('2024'), PART P2 VALUES('2023'))

codes.d: Duplicate keyword specified in the statement.
codes.a: Same option appears twice in a DDL or DML statement.
codes.f: Remove the duplicate keyword.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T (C1 INT NOT NULL NOT NULL);

codes.d: CREATE TABLE does not include any column definitions.
codes.a: CREATE TABLE statement is missing column list.
codes.f: Add at least one column.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T;

codes.t: NULLABLE COLUMN CANNOT BE IN PARTITION KEY
codes.d: A nullable column has been specified in the partitioning key.
codes.a: Partitioning key column was defined NULL.
codes.f: Alter the column to NOT NULL or change partitioning key.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T (C1 INT) PARTITION BY (C1);  /* C1 nullable */

codes.d: LOCKSIZE ROW cannot be specified because not supported for this tablespace.
codes.a: Type 1 indexes or older tablespace types disallow row locking.
codes.f: Use LOCKSIZE ANY or LOCKSIZE PAGE; convert TS to UTS for row locks.
codes.x: CREATE TABLESPACE TS1 LOCKSIZE ROW;  /* old TS type */

codes.d: COMPRESS YES is not allowed for this tablespace.
codes.a: Compression unsupported for tablespace type or page size.
codes.f: Use a supported tablespace type or remove COMPRESS YES.
codes.x: CREATE TABLESPACE TS1 LOB COMPRESS YES;

codes.t: TOO MANY COLUMNS IN A UNIQUE CONSTRAINT
codes.d: Number of columns specified for the UNIQUE constraint exceeds the limit.
codes.a: UNIQUE has more columns than DB2 allows.
codes.f: Reduce the number of columns in the constraint.
codes.x: UNIQUE (C1, C2, ..., C65)

codes.d: The text of a check constraint exceeds the maximum allowable size.
codes.a: CHECK condition text > 3800 bytes.
codes.f: Simplify or split into multiple constraints.
codes.x: CHECK (C1 IN ('A','B', ...thousands of values...))

codes.d: Invalid value specified for keyword in DDL statement.
codes.a: Unsupported value for an option (e.g., LOCKMAX -1).
codes.f: Use a valid value per SQL Reference.
codes.x: CREATE TABLESPACE TS1 LOCKMAX -1;

codes.t: WHERE NOT NULL CANNOT BE USED ON A NULL COLUMN
codes.d: WHERE NOT NULL cannot be specified because none of the columns are nullable.
codes.a: Specified WHERE NOT NULL on index but no nullable columns.
codes.f: Drop the WHERE NOT NULL clause.
codes.x: CREATE INDEX IX1 ON T(C1) WHERE C1 IS NOT NULL;  /* C1 NOT NULL */

codes.t: TABLE CANNOT BE CREATED IN THE TABLESPACE
codes.d: Table cannot be created in the specified tablespace because it is partitioned/LOB.
codes.a: Trying to put a table in a LOB or AUX tablespace, or wrong TS type.
codes.f: Use a tablespace appropriate for the table type.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T IN DB1.TS_LOB (C1 INT);

codes.t: BUFFERPOOL DOES NOT EXIST OR IS NOT ACTIVATED
codes.d: The bufferpool specified for the tablespace or index space has not been activated.
codes.a: Referenced bufferpool not configured or sized 0.
codes.f: Activate or create bufferpool via DB2 commands.
codes.x: CREATE TABLESPACE TS1 BUFFERPOOL BP99;  /* BP99 not active */

codes.t: FOREIGN KEY CANNOT BE DEFINED ON A TABLE THAT IS NOT IN THE SAME DATABASE
codes.d: Foreign key cannot be defined because the parent table is in another database.
codes.a: Cross-database FK not allowed.
codes.f: Move tables to the same database or use triggers for cross-DB integrity.
codes.x: FOREIGN KEY (DEPT) REFERENCES OTHERDB.DEPT;

codes.t: DELETE RULE CANNOT BE ALTERED — TABLE HAS TRIGGERS
codes.d: Delete rule cannot be altered because the table has a delete trigger.
codes.a: Conflict between FK delete rule and trigger semantics.
codes.f: DROP the trigger or change delete rule first.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ALTER FK ON DELETE CASCADE;  /* delete trigger exists */

codes.d: Table cannot be altered for the specified reason.
codes.a: Tablespace state or table attributes block the alter.
codes.f: Check tablespace status; coordinate with DBA.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD COLUMN C1 INT;  /* TS REORG pending */

codes.d: Table description has reached maximum descriptive size.
codes.a: Internal SYSTABLES record exceeded size limit (e.g., too many columns/constraints).
codes.f: Reduce columns/constraints, or split into multiple tables.
codes.x: Table with 1000+ columns and many constraints.

codes.d: Row violates an installation-defined edit or validation procedure.
codes.a: VALIDPROC or EDITPROC rejected the row.
codes.f: Adjust input data per installation rules.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP ... ;  /* VALIDPROC rejects */

codes.t: TABLE IN PARTITIONED TABLESPACE NOT AVAILABLE BECAUSE INDEX NOT EXIST
codes.d: Table in a partitioned tablespace is not available because its partitioning index has not been created.
codes.a: Partitioned table created but no partitioning index yet.
codes.f: Create the partitioning index to bring the table online.
codes.x: INSERT INTO PARTITIONED_T VALUES (...);  /* missing PI */

codes.d: Table size exceeds maximum allowed.
codes.a: Table reached DSSIZE limit.
codes.f: Repartition or use larger DSSIZE.
codes.x: INSERT INTO HUGE_TABLE VALUES (...);  /* reached limit */

codes.t: ALTER STOGROUP STATEMENT IS INVALID BECAUSE A LIST CONTAINS NON-EMPTY VOLUMES
codes.d: ALTER STOGROUP cannot remove volumes that contain data.
codes.a: Volume specified for removal still holds data.
codes.f: REORG/move data off the volume before removing.
codes.x: ALTER STOGROUP SG1 REMOVE VOLUMES (VOL1);

codes.t: FOREIGN KEY CANNOT BE DEFINED ON A SELF-REFERENCING TABLE WITH DELETE SET NULL
codes.d: Self-referencing constraint cannot have DELETE SET NULL because the foreign key column is part of the primary key.
codes.a: Self-ref FK column overlaps with PK, conflicting with SET NULL.
codes.f: Use DELETE CASCADE or RESTRICT.
codes.x: FOREIGN KEY (EMPNO) REFERENCES EMP(EMPNO) ON DELETE SET NULL;

codes.d: USING VCAT cannot be specified for the partition specification because the catalog name is implicit.
codes.a: VCAT specified where DB2 controls storage group.
codes.f: Use USING STOGROUP or omit USING VCAT.
codes.x: PARTITION 1 USING VCAT MYVCAT;

codes.t: DROP NOT ALLOWED ON A TABLE WITH MQT
codes.d: DROP cannot be processed because the table has materialized query tables defined on it.
codes.a: Underlying base table can't be dropped while MQT depends on it.
codes.f: DROP MQTs first, then DROP base.
codes.x: DROP TABLE EMP;  /* MQT depends on EMP */

codes.d: Object reached its maximum size.
codes.a: Partition size or VSAM data set size limit reached.
codes.f: Increase DSSIZE or repartition.
codes.x: INSERT into table partition exceeding 64GB size.

codes.t: INDEX CANNOT BE PARTITIONED — NO CORRESPONDING PARTITION KEY
codes.d: Partitioning index has no corresponding partition key.
codes.a: PARTITION specified for an index whose key doesn't match table partitioning.
codes.f: Use CREATE INDEX without PART or match table partitioning.
codes.x: CREATE INDEX IX1 ON EMP(NAME) PART 1 VALUES ('M');

codes.t: INDEX HAS WRONG NUMBER OF PARTITIONS
codes.d: The number of partitions specified for the index does not match the number of partitions for the table.
codes.a: PARTITION count mismatch between table and partitioning index.
codes.f: Match partition count in CREATE INDEX.
codes.x: CREATE INDEX IX1 ON EMP_PART (5 partitions) PART 3;

codes.t: PARTITIONED TABLE SPACE CANNOT BE USED
codes.d: Partitioned tablespace cannot be used because no partitioning index has been defined.
codes.a: Table moved to partitioned TS without partitioning index.
codes.f: Define partitioning index immediately after creating table.
codes.x: INSERT INTO EMP_PART VALUES (...);

codes.t: NUMBER OF KEY LIMIT VALUES NOT VALID
codes.d: Number of key limit values for partition does not match the number of columns of the partitioning key.
codes.a: Partition boundary specifies wrong number of column values.
codes.f: Provide one value per partitioning key column.
codes.x: PARTITION 1 VALUES ('A');  /* PK has 2 columns */

codes.t: PARTITIONING KEY LIMIT EXCEEDS COLUMN LENGTH
codes.d: Internal length of limit-key fields for the partitioning index exceeds the column length.
codes.a: Limit value too long for column data type.
codes.f: Use shorter limit values within column length.
codes.x: PART 1 VALUES ('TOOLONGSTRING') for CHAR(5)

codes.t: PART CLAUSE OF AN ALTER STATEMENT IS NOT VALID
codes.d: PART clause specified for an ALTER is not valid for the tablespace.
codes.a: PART option used on non-partitioned tablespace.
codes.f: Use PART only with partitioned tablespaces.
codes.x: ALTER TABLESPACE TS1 PART 2 USING STOGROUP SG2;

codes.t: OPERATION CANNOT BE EXECUTED WHILE UTILITY IS IN PROGRESS
codes.d: Statement cannot be executed because a utility is in progress.
codes.a: DDL/DML attempted while REORG, RUNSTATS, COPY, etc. holds the resource.
codes.f: Wait for utility completion or terminate utility.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD COL X INT;  /* REORG in progress */

codes.t: DROP/ALTER INVALID — CLUSTERING INDEX MUST EXIST
codes.d: The clustering index for a partitioned tablespace cannot be dropped.
codes.a: DROP INDEX on the partitioning/clustering index of partitioned TS.
codes.f: Create new clustering index first, or drop tablespace.
codes.x: DROP INDEX IX_PART_CLUSTER;

codes.t: COLUMN CANNOT BE ADDED — TABLE HAS EDITPROC OR VALIDPROC
codes.d: Column cannot be added because the table has an EDITPROC or VALIDPROC.
codes.a: Edit/validation procedure prevents adding columns.
codes.f: Remove EDITPROC/VALIDPROC, alter, then restore.
codes.x: ALTER TABLE EMP ADD COL X INT;  /* EDITPROC defined */

codes.d: Table cannot be explicitly dropped from a partitioned tablespace.
codes.a: Trying to DROP TABLE from partitioned TS containing only that table.
codes.f: Use DROP TABLESPACE which drops contained tables.
codes.x: DROP TABLE PART_EMP;

codes.d: The record length of the table exceeds the page size limit.
codes.a: Sum of column lengths exceeds 4K/8K/16K/32K page capacity.
codes.f: Use larger page size tablespace; reduce column lengths; use LOB/CLOB.
codes.x: CREATE TABLE T (C1 CHAR(32000)) IN 4K TS;

codes.d: Bufferpool of the tablespace cannot be changed.
codes.a: ALTER TABLESPACE BUFFERPOOL change not supported in this context.
codes.f: DROP/recreate tablespace, or use supported bufferpool ALTER path.
codes.x: ALTER TABLESPACE TS1 BUFFERPOOL BP2;

codes.t: OPERATION DROP NOT ALLOWED ON TABLE
codes.d: DROP TABLE failed because RESTRICT ON DROP was specified.
codes.a: Table created or altered WITH RESTRICT ON DROP.
codes.f: ALTER TABLE ... NOT RESTRICT ON DROP first, then DROP.
codes.x: DROP TABLE EMP;  /* RESTRICT ON DROP */

codes.d: An inserted or updated value is invalid because the index limits entries to unique values.
codes.a: Duplicate value violates a UNIQUE INDEX or PRIMARY KEY constraint.
codes.f: Check if the row already exists before inserting. Use MERGE for upsert behavior. SELECT first or handle SQLCODE -803 in the program.
codes.x:
EXEC SQL
   INSERT INTO EMP(EMPNO, NAME)
   VALUES (:EMPNO, :NAME)
END-EXEC.
IF SQLCODE = -803
   DISPLAY 'EMPLOYEE ALREADY EXISTS'.

codes.t: DBRM OR PACKAGE NOT FOUND IN PLAN
codes.d: The DBRM or package name was not found in the plan.
codes.a: Program's package wasn't bound, or bound under a different collection ID than runtime.
codes.f: BIND PACKAGE for the program. Check CURRENT PACKAGESET and plan PKLIST. Verify collection ID matches.
codes.x: BIND PACKAGE(MYCOLL) MEMBER(MYPGM) OWNER(USER1);

codes.t: MORE THAN ONE ROW RETURNED BY SCALAR SUBQUERY
codes.d: The result of an embedded SELECT INTO or scalar subquery is more than one row.
codes.a: Singleton SELECT returned multiple rows but program expected one.
codes.f: Use a cursor (DECLARE/OPEN/FETCH) for multi-row results. Or refine the WHERE clause with a unique key.
codes.x:
EXEC SQL
   SELECT NAME INTO :NAME
   FROM EMP WHERE DEPT = 'A00'
END-EXEC.   *> multiple rows - use cursor

codes.t: TIMESTAMP MISMATCH BETWEEN LOAD MODULE AND DBRM
codes.d: The precompiler-generated timestamp X in the load module is different from the bind timestamp Y in the DBRM.
codes.a: Program was recompiled but not rebound, or vice versa.
codes.f: Precompile, compile, link, AND bind together. Always rebind after precompiling.
codes.x: Run sequence: DSNHPC -> COBOL -> LINK -> BIND PLAN(myplan)

codes.t: DB2 ENCOUNTERED AN INVALID VALUE IN THE CATALOG
codes.d: DB2 detected an invalid value in a catalog column during initialization or migration.
codes.a: Corrupt catalog data, often from incomplete migration or maintenance.
codes.f: Run DSN1COPY/REPAIR or apply the appropriate maintenance APAR. Contact IBM support.
codes.x: DB2 startup error or random failures on a single table.

codes.t: TOO MANY ITEMS RETURNED IN A SELECT OR INSERT LIST
codes.d: Too many items returned in a SELECT list, INSERT list, or values list.
codes.a: More than 750 items in a SELECT or INSERT list.
codes.f: Reduce the number of items; split the operation.
codes.x: SELECT C1, C2, ..., C800 FROM T;

codes.d: The application process is not connected to an application server.
codes.a: No active DB2 connection (e.g., after CONNECT RESET or before initial CONNECT).
codes.f: Issue CONNECT TO before SQL.
codes.x: EXEC SQL SELECT 1 FROM SYSIBM.SYSDUMMY1 END-EXEC.  /* no CONNECT */

codes.d: Unsuccessful execution caused by an unavailable resource.
codes.a: Tablespace in COPY-pending, LPL, restricted state, or other resource lock.
codes.f: Check the reason code and resource name in the message. Run COPY, RECOVER, START DATABASE, or similar to recover.
codes.x:
Reason 00C90081 - tablespace in COPY-pending.
-START DATABASE(MYDB) SPACENAM(MYTS)

codes.d: Unsuccessful execution due to resource limit being exceeded.
codes.a: Query exceeded RLF (Resource Limit Facility) CPU/time threshold for the user/plan.
codes.f: Tune the query, use better access path, or have admin raise the RLF limit.
codes.x: Dynamic SQL exceeds DSNRLST limit for the plan.

codes.t: SQL STATEMENT CANNOT BE EXECUTED — PRIOR ERROR
codes.d: The SQL statement cannot be executed because this function is disabled due to a prior error.
codes.a: Prior critical SQL error left the unit of work in unusable state.
codes.f: ROLLBACK the unit of work and start fresh.
codes.x: After -911, more SQL returns -906 until ROLLBACK.

codes.t: SCHEMA OR DATABASE HAS BEEN MODIFIED
codes.d: The DDL statement cannot be executed because the schema or database was modified.
codes.a: Concurrent DDL changed schema mid-transaction.
codes.f: Retry the transaction.
codes.x: Two threads ALTER same table concurrently.

codes.t: BIND, REBIND, OR AUTO-REBIND NOT ALLOWED
codes.d: The BIND/REBIND/AUTO-REBIND operation is not allowed.
codes.a: DB2 install set BIND NEW PACKAGE=NO, or thread restriction.
codes.f: Verify install options; coordinate with sysprog to allow binds.
codes.x: BIND PACKAGE(MYCOLL) MEMBER(PGM);

codes.t: STATEMENT CANNOT ACCESS RESOURCE — UNCOMMITTED CHANGE PENDING
codes.d: SQL statement cannot access an object that has a pending DROP.
codes.a: Object dropped/altered in same UOW; system can't access it until COMMIT.
codes.f: COMMIT first or do not attempt to access pending-drop objects.
codes.x: DROP TABLE T; SELECT * FROM T;  /* same UOW */

codes.d: The current unit of work was rolled back because of a deadlock or timeout.
codes.a: Lock contention or held resource exceeded timeout (IRLM resource limit, often 30-60s).
codes.f: Application must restart the unit of work. Use LOCK TIMEOUT bind option. Reduce hold time by COMMITting more frequently.
codes.x: Reason code 00C9008E = timeout, 00C90088 = deadlock. Application should retry with backoff.

codes.t: MAX NUMBER OF LOCKS REACHED — DEADLOCK
codes.d: The maximum number of locks has been reached, transaction was rolled back.
codes.a: Single transaction accumulated too many locks (NUMLKUS exceeded).
codes.f: COMMIT more often, use LOCKSIZE TABLESPACE to escalate, or raise NUMLKUS in DSNZPARM.
codes.x: Long-running batch updates millions of rows without intermediate COMMIT.

codes.d: Unsuccessful execution caused by deadlock or timeout, but no rollback was performed.
codes.a: Lock contention; bind option NORLBE prevents rollback on -911.
codes.f: Application must explicitly ROLLBACK and retry.
codes.x: IMS or CICS attach with NORLBE option encounters lock conflict.

codes.d: SQL statement cannot be executed because a connection has been lost.
codes.a: DDF outage or network problem; remote subsystem dropped.
codes.f: Application should ROLLBACK, reconnect, and retry.
codes.x: Network blip between client and DB2 DDF causes connection loss.

codes.d: A rollback operation is required.
codes.a: Atomic statement failed; thread must rollback.
codes.f: ROLLBACK and retry.
codes.x: Multi-row INSERT failed atomically.

codes.d: Authorization failure: error code returned by authorization routine.
codes.a: User authentication failed, RACF/security exit rejected, or expired password.
codes.f: Check user ID/password. Validate RACF profile. Check DB2 security exit.
codes.x: JDBC connection with expired password.

codes.d: Connection not established because DB2 not active, MAXIMUM users exceeded, or related issue.
codes.a: DB2 down, IRLM not active, or thread limits reached.
codes.f: Check DB2 startup, IRLM, and MAX USERS/MAX BATCH settings.
codes.x: Reason 00E70005 = DB2 not started.

codes.d: DB2 connection internal error.
codes.a: Internal DB2 connection problem with attach facility (TSO, CICS, IMS, RRS).
codes.f: Check the function, return code, and reason code in the SQLERRMC. Often requires sysprog intervention.
codes.x: CICS attach failure during DB2 restart.

codes.t: COMMIT NOT VALID IN IMS/CICS ENVIRONMENT
codes.d: COMMIT not valid in this environment.
codes.a: SQL COMMIT issued under IMS or CICS, which use their own transaction managers.
codes.f: Use EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT or IMS commit verbs; do not use SQL COMMIT.
codes.x: EXEC SQL COMMIT END-EXEC.  /* in CICS program */

codes.t: ROLLBACK NOT VALID IN IMS/CICS ENVIRONMENT
codes.d: ROLLBACK not valid in this environment.
codes.a: SQL ROLLBACK issued under IMS or CICS.
codes.f: Use EXEC CICS SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK or IMS rollback verbs.
codes.x: EXEC SQL ROLLBACK END-EXEC.  /* in CICS */

codes.t: LANGUAGE INTERFACE WAS CALLED FOR ESTABLISHING IMPLICIT CONNECTION
codes.d: Language interface was called when DB2 was not yet established.
codes.a: Program tried SQL before TSO/batch attach was set up.
codes.f: Use DSN RUN command or correct CAF/RRSAF call sequence.
codes.x: Batch JCL with PGM=MYPROG missing DSN SYSTEM(DB2A) RUN.

codes.t: ROLLBACK REQUIRED DUE TO UNREQUESTED ROLLBACK
codes.d: Rollback required due to an unrequested rollback at the remote site.
codes.a: Two-phase commit partner forced rollback.
codes.f: ROLLBACK locally and retry.
codes.x: Distributed unit of work where remote DB2 forced rollback.

codes.t: STATEMENT FAILED — UPDATE OF SYSTEM CATALOG IN PROGRESS
codes.d: SQL statement failed because the system catalog is being updated.
codes.a: Catalog quiesce or upgrade in progress.
codes.f: Wait for catalog operation to complete.
codes.x: SELECT during DB2 catalog migration.

codes.d: Distributed operation is invalid.
codes.a: DDF disabled or operation not supported between sites.
codes.f: Enable DDF or restructure to avoid the distributed op.
codes.x: Update at multiple sites in a single UOW without DDF.

codes.t: LOCATION NAME NOT IN COMMUNICATIONS DATABASE
codes.d: Location name specified in the CONNECT statement is invalid or undefined.
codes.a: Location not in SYSIBM.LOCATIONS or BSDS doesn't define it.
codes.f: Add location to communications database (SYSIBM.LOCATIONS) and update BSDS.
codes.x: CONNECT TO REMOTE_DB;  /* not defined */

codes.d: An operation exception was detected — the program tried to execute an invalid machine instruction.
codes.a: Branched to an area without valid code (zeros, data, deleted load module). Often caused by stale module pointer or overlay of executable code.
codes.f: Check the PSW and offset in the abend dump. Verify the program was linked correctly and the entry point exists. Check for storage overlays.
codes.x:
PSW at abend: 078D1000 80001234
*> Branched into a CSECT of zeros at offset X'1234'

codes.d: The program attempted to access storage it is not authorized to read or write.
codes.a: Reference through an uninitialized or invalid pointer, walking off the end of an array, or accessing storage from a different key.
codes.f: Look at the PSW and failing instruction in the IPCS dump. Trace the pointer back to where it was set.
codes.x: MVC  DEST,0(R3)     *> R3 contains X'00000000' from cleared field

codes.d: A decimal arithmetic instruction encountered invalid packed-decimal or zoned-decimal data.
codes.a: An input field contained spaces, low-values, or non-numeric characters where COBOL expected a numeric value. Common after reading uninitialized records.
